# IPsec PCAP dataset v1.0

## Provenance and scope

This imported snapshot contains 239 classic Ethernet PCAPs and 239 corresponding
rows in `metadata.csv`. It was generated by the isolated Docker/strongSwan lab in
the dedicated `ipsec-pcap-lab` repository. Twenty historical captures are
preserved byte-for-byte within the current layout; the source repository protects
them with a separate SHA-256 inventory.

Captures were taken from the outer side of the IPsec peers. Application payloads
remain protected by native ESP or UDP/4500-encapsulated ESP. No preprocessing
step decrypts ESP or derives labels from filenames or packet features.

## Dataset roles

| Role | Count | Labels or scenarios |
|---|---:|---|
| `train_known` | 175 | 25 each of web, video, VoIP, email, file transfer, messaging, and ICMP |
| `ood_eval` | 25 | DNS, SSH, gaming UDP, database, and remote desktop; all map to `IGNORE` |
| `anomaly_eval` | 30 | ICMP flood, UDP flood, and beacon burst; all map to `IGNORE` |
| `protocol_validation` | 5 | One negotiation-first IKE/ESP session per profile; maps to `IGNORE` |
| `archived_provenance` | 4 | Historical OOD captures under `pcaps/ood/archive/`; maps to `IGNORE` |

Only `train_known` is eligible for supervised classifier construction. The
`split` field is authoritative for known records: R01-R03 are `train`, R04 is
`validation`, and R05 is `locked_test`. For every other dataset role, the role
and `IGNORE` label override the legacy `split` value; those records are excluded
from classifier fitting regardless of what that field contains.

## Capture matrix

The known matrix is complete at 7 classes x 5 profiles x 5 runs:

- P01: IKEv2, IPv4 tunnel, AES-128-CBC plus HMAC-SHA256, native ESP, PFS off.
- P02: IKEv2, IPv4 tunnel, AES-256-GCM, ECP256, forced UDP/4500, PFS off.
- P03: IKEv1, IPv4 tunnel, AES-256-CBC plus HMAC-SHA256, MODP2048, native ESP,
  PFS on.
- P04: IKEv1, IPv4 transport, AES-128-CBC plus HMAC-SHA256, MODP3072, forced
  UDP/4500, PFS on.
- P05: IKEv2, IPv6 tunnel, AES-256-CBC plus HMAC-SHA384, ECP384, native ESP,
  PFS off.

P02 and P04 deliberately use `forceencaps=yes`. This proves UDP/4500 handling,
not real NAT traversal. Every metadata row correctly records
`actual_nat_present=no`, and every peer uses PSK authentication.

OOD evaluation contains one capture for each of five unsupported traffic types
across each profile. Anomaly evaluation contains two independent captures per
profile for each of three anomaly types, for ten captures per anomaly type.

## Metadata schema

`metadata.csv` preserves source labels and configuration facts while adding:

- canonical label and dataset role;
- authoritative `pcap_path`;
- profile, run, and split identifiers;
- packet-derived capture start/end timestamps and observed span;
- packet count, PCAP file size, and captured frame bytes;
- capture interface and link type;
- JSON generator parameters and tool versions;
- SHA-256 and anomaly annotations;
- protocol facts for the five protocol-validation sessions.

Identifiers, paths, source labels, profiles, run numbers, addresses, timestamps,
generator names, and cryptographic settings are audit-only metadata and must not
be model features.

## Frozen manifest and validation

`dataset-manifest-v1.0.csv` contains a header plus 239 data rows. It was produced
only after the source repository's strict validator passed. The manifest records:

`dataset_version`, `pcap_path`, `sha256`, `canonical_label`, `original_label`,
`profile_id`, `run_id`, `dataset_role`, `split`, `packet_count`,
`observed_packet_span_s`, `pcap_file_size_bytes`, `capture_started_at_utc`, and
`capture_ended_at_utc`.

The source validator checks missing or extra captures, duplicate IDs and hashes,
hash and packet-statistic mismatches, JSON fields, labels and roles, profile/run
coverage, anomaly/OOD counts, and native ESP versus UDP/4500 profile semantics.

## ML-readiness limitation

All 175 known captures are readable by the current adapter and produce 591 flow
windows, but window contribution is not balanced:

| Class | Extracted windows |
|---|---:|
| web | 28 |
| email | 45 |
| icmp | 47 |
| file_transfer | 59 |
| video | 64 |
| voip | 149 |
| messaging | 199 |

Observed duration is correlated with class: web has a median span near 3.33
seconds, while VoIP and messaging have medians near 52.42 and 73.73 seconds.
This can create a traffic-generator shortcut. Before model selection, the main
pipeline must preserve capture groups and declared splits, use equal numbers of
complete windows per capture, evaluate performance without suspicious duration
features, and run the dataset-leakage audit. Future collection should sustain
each known class for a common active duration.

## Coverage not claimed

This version does not provide evidence for:

- real NAT traversal;
- certificate-based peer authentication;
- IKE SA or CHILD SA rekey and key-lifetime expiry;
- deliberate replay-window or replay-protection behavior;
- normal non-IPsec negative traffic;
- AH traffic, which remains optional for the MVP.

Some historical captures contain ordinary ESP reordering and must not be used as
replay-protection proof. The data is synthetic and lab-only. The MVP assumes one
dominant known application type per capture/window and does not claim perfect
separation of simultaneous inner applications inside an opaque site-to-site
tunnel.
